{{nihongo|'''Ato Shrine'''|阿刀神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamashiro Province]].

{{List of coordinates}}
'''Ato Shrine''' (あとじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} located in Saga Hirosawa Minaminocho, {{ill|Ukyō-ku, Kyoto|Q580186|qid=Q580186}}, {{ill|Kyoto|Q34600|qid=Q34600}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|Q120730|qid=Q120730}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}, and under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|lt=former shrine ranking}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}.

=== Enshrined deity ===
According to the “Shrine Register” of {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 16 ({{ill|1883|Q7816|qid=Q7816}}), the enshrined deity is {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Ōmikami}}{{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1979}}. On the other hand, the “Jingishi Shiryō” states that the enshrined deity is Ato no Sukune’s ancestral deity, Aji Nuta no Mikoto ({{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ajinuta no Mikoto}}){{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1979}}.

There is also a theory that the shrine name “Ato” derives from “Atsu,” that is, “Yatsu (valley),” through phonetic change, and that the enshrined deity is a water deity (= an agricultural deity){{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1979}}.

=== History ===
=== Overview ===
[[File:Atobe-jinja (Yao), torii.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Atobe Shrine ({{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}{{ill|Yao, Osaka|Q490872|qid=Q490872}})}}]]
As suggested by the shrine name “Ato,” this shrine is regarded as the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655|lt=ujigami shrine}} of the ancient clan {{ill|Ato clan|Q17191532|qid=Q17191532}}{{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. Regarding the Ato clan, the “{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}” ({{ill|815|Q29917|qid=Q29917}}) records “Ato no Sukune” and “Ato no Muraji” in Yamashiro Province, stating that they were branch families of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Isonokami no Ason}} ({{ill|Mononobe clan|Q1755836|qid=Q1755836}}) and descendants of Aji Nuta no Mikoto, a grandson of {{ill|Nigihayahi|Q10949054|qid=Q10949054}}{{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. The original base of the Ato clan was Atobe in {{ill|Shibukawa district|Q11561609|qid=Q11561609}}, {{ill|Kawachi Province|Q1047150|qid=Q1047150}} (around present-day {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Atobe Shrine}} in {{ill|Yao, Osaka|Q490872|qid=Q490872}}, {{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}), but it is said that with the relocation of the capital to {{ill|Heian-kyō|Q751907|qid=Q751907}}, they migrated and transferred their ancestral deity to this area{{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}.

In the {{ill|Rikkokushi|Q1151168|qid=Q1151168|lt=national histories}}, in {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 8 ({{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}})<ref group="Original">“Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku,” Jōgan 8 (866), intercalary 3rd month, 7th day.</ref>, a divine rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower was bestowed upon what appears to be the Ato deity, recorded as “Furui-gami”{{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}. In addition, the “{{ill|Nihon Kōki|Q1077029|qid=Q1077029}}”<ref group="Original">“Nihon Kōki,” Enryaku 23 (804), 2nd month, 5th day.</ref> states that “the ritual implements of {{ill|Isonokami Jingū|Q708859|qid=Q708859}} in Yamato Province were transferred to Katsuno District, Yamashiro Province,” and it is said that this place was a small shrine called “Shingū no Yashiro” that existed northwest of Ato Shrine (Saga Shingūcho) until the Meiji period{{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}} (no longer extant{{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1979}}).

In the “{{ill|Engishiki|Q1342448|qid=Q1342448}}” {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Register of Deities}}, compiled in {{ill|Enchō|Q1327274|qid=Q1327274|lt=Engi}} 5 ({{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), “Ato Shrine” is listed in {{ill|Kadono district|Q13579879|qid=Q13579879}}, {{ill|Yamashiro Province|cs|Provincie Jamaširo|de|Provinz Yamashiro|es|Provincia de Yamashiro|fa|ولایت یاماشیرو|fr|Province de Yamashiro|gl|Provincia de Yamashiro|hak|Yamashiro-koet|id|Provinsi Yamashiro|it|Yamashiro (provincia)|ja|山城国|ko|야마시로국|lt|Jamaširo žemė|ms|Yamashiro Province|nl|Yamashiro (provincie)|pt|Província de Yamashiro|ru|Ямасиро (провинция)|simple|Yamashiro Province|sk|Jamaširo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Јамаширо|tr|Yamashiro (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ямашіро|wuu|山城国|zh|山城國|zh_min_nan|Yamasiro-kok|zh_yue|山城國|qid=Q749276}}, and it is ranked as a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}}{{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Heibonsha)|1979}}.

In {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}} 10 ({{ill|1877|Q7773|qid=Q7773}}), March, under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Q712534|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}, it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|Q134917284|qid=Q134917284}}{{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1979}}. At present, only a small shrine remains.

=== Divine ranks ===
* {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 8 ({{ill|866|Q23872|qid=Q23872}}), intercalary 3rd month, 7th day: promoted from Senior Sixth Rank, Upper to Junior Fifth Rank, Lower (“{{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Q1052981|qid=Q1052981}}”). The notation is “Furui-gami,” and manuscripts contain a marginal note “Ato,” which is taken to indicate this shrine{{Sfn|Ato Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1979}}.
